feature.name: secrets-environment-bundles
feature.summary: Introduce configurable, governance-tiered secret 'bundles' (independent/developer/release) so a developer submits secrets for multiple related environments in one atomic commit and PR, with server-enforced bundle membership and a release-control signal for external PR-review/CODEOWNERS gating.

acceptance_criteria: GET /api/secrets/apps returns bundleId per app/environment entry and a top-level bundles catalog (id, displayName, order, releaseControlled), derived only from data/secretBundles.json
A bundle tab is shown only when at least one of its declared environments is actually deployed for the selected app; bundles with zero matching deployed environments are omitted entirely

Pre-flight per-environment eligibility (vault/qualifier ambiguity) is resolved client-side via the existing GET /api/secrets/:appName/:environment endpoint, called once per bundle-member-and-deployed environment, before submission is enabled

POST /api/secrets bundle-mode request is rejected with 400 if bundleId is unknown or any submitted environment is not a declared member of that bundle, verified server-side independent of any client-supplied claim
A bundle submission that omits a currently-eligible (unambiguous) declared environment is rejected with 400 INCOMPLETE_BUNDLE and produces zero writes

A successful bundle submission produces exactly one Git commit and one pull request covering every included environment's secrets.enc.yaml file, using the Git Data API (createTree/createCommit/createRef-or-updateRef)
Any failure during eligibility resolution, encryption, or pre-write conflict detection aborts the entire submission with zero GitHub writes
A PR-creation failure after a successful commit returns 500 PR_CREATION_FAILED with the branchName and commitSha, and is never automatically retried

Two structurally identical bundle submissions (same target, appName, bundleId, included environments, vault/qualifier selections, and secret names) while a PR is open are rejected with 409 PR_EXISTS and no additional writes; a structurally distinct submission for the same app+bundle succeeds even while another PR is open
A developer can enter a different secret value per environment for the same secret name within one bundle submission, and no value is copied across environments

A releaseControlled bundle's PR title carries a [RELEASE] prefix and its PR body and audit log carry a release-control marker, always derived server-side from data/secretBundles.json, never from client input
No secretValue ever appears in logs, commit messages, PR titles/bodies, or validator error responses, including within the new environmentSecrets[].secrets[].secretValue nested validator path
All existing single-environment and legacy multi-environment (environments[]) secret submission behavior continues to pass unmodified

user_stories.as: developer submitting secrets for a release
user_stories.i_want: to submit one set of per-environment secret values across all environments in the Release Bundle in a single action
user_stories.so_that: the change lands as one auditable, atomically-committed PR instead of several disconnected ones
acceptance_criteria: Selecting the Release Bundle tab shows only the bundle's environments that are actually deployed for the selected app
Submitting produces exactly one PR referencing all included environments' files
The PR title and body clearly indicate this is a release-controlled change

user_stories.as: developer whose app has an ambiguous Key Vault in one bundle environment
user_stories.i_want: to see that environment excluded with a clear reason and a way to disambiguate it, without blocking the rest of the bundle
user_stories.so_that: I can still submit for every other eligible environment in one action
acceptance_criteria: The ambiguous environment renders disabled with a specific reason (multiple vaults or multiple qualifiers)
Supplying vaultDir/qualifier for that one environment makes it eligible without affecting other environments
Submission proceeds for the remaining eligible environments if the ambiguous one is left excluded

user_stories.i_want: to add, rename, reorder, or move an environment between bundles by editing one JSON config file
user_stories.so_that: no code deployment is required to reconfigure which environments belong to which bundle
acceptance_criteria: Editing data/secretBundles.json and merging it is sufficient to change bundle membership/order/display name
An invalid edit (duplicate id, environment in two bundles) is rejected and the last-known-good configuration continues to serve requests
A missing or unparseable config at cold start causes bundle-aware reads to show no bundle membership and bundle-mode submissions to fail closed with 503

flows.name: Bundle-scoped read and pre-flight eligibility
steps: Developer selects target and app; frontend calls GET /api/secrets/apps (unchanged call shape)

Backend calls loadSecretBundles(correlationId) exactly once for this request, then attaches bundleId per entry (via classifyBundleMembership(env, bundleConfig), a pure function over the once-loaded config, not a per-entry re-read) and a bundles catalog (via getBundleCatalog(bundleConfig)) derived from the same loaded config
Frontend groups entries by bundleId filtered to the selected app; omits any catalog bundle with zero matching entries
Developer selects a bundle tab; frontend calls GET /api/secrets/:appName/:environment once per candidate environment, in parallel
Frontend classifies each environment as eligible or excluded (with reason); submit stays disabled until at least one is eligible

error_paths.handling: bundles catalog returns empty array; all bundleId fields are null; UI shows only the legacy All Environments tab

error_paths.error: GitHub API failure on a per-environment pre-flight call
error_paths.handling: that environment is treated as excluded with the error message as the reason; other environments' calls are unaffected

flows.name: Atomic bundle submission
steps: Frontend POSTs bundleId + environmentSecrets[] + jiraTicket to POST /api/secrets

Backend validates request shape/size via the 3-way oneOf() validator dispatch (branch A: legacy secrets[], branch B: legacy secretName/secretValue, branch C: bundleId+environmentSecrets[]), then the route-level 3-way exactly-one check (hasSingular/hasArray/hasBundle) routes matching requests to handleBundleSecretsSubmission() before any legacy-path logic runs
Backend validates bundle membership server-side (validateBundleMembership, its own single loadSecretBundles(correlationId) call for this request)
Backend re-resolves eligibility server-side across the full declared bundle membership (resolveBundleEnvironments)
Backend computes bundleContentHash and checks findOpenPullRequest for the resulting deterministic branch name
Backend captures each included environment's file SHA (pre-encryption)
Backend encrypts every secret for every included environment (chunked concurrency, abort-all on first failure)
Backend re-checks each included environment's file SHA (post-encryption, pre-write); the resulting SHAs become expectedFileShas

Backend builds one Git tree, one commit, and one branch ref (createMultiFileCommit), which itself re-reads expectedFileShas as a final write-time CAS check immediately before createTree, and maps a createRef/updateRef 422 ref race to the same CONFLICT code

Backend creates one pull request (title carries [RELEASE] prefix and body carries the release marker if releaseControlled); correlationId threads through createMultiFileCommit and createPullRequest, and submitSecretBundleViaGitOps emits its own [correlationId][bundle:bundleId]-tagged phase lines throughout
Backend responds with included/excluded environments, secretCount, and PR details

error_scenarios.scenario: A target file's SHA drifts between the caller's own pre-encryption capture and its post-encryption re-check (concurrent modification, caught before createMultiFileCommit is even called)
error_scenarios.handling: Abort the entire bundle submission; no writes occur; no automatic retry
error_scenarios.user_message: The target file changed since this submission started. Please retry.

error_scenarios.scenario: A target file's SHA drifts between the caller's post-encryption re-check and createMultiFileCommit's own internal write-time CAS re-read, OR createRef/updateRef returns 422 because a concurrent request created/moved the same branch (Round 1 Blocking Finding 2)
error_scenarios.handling: createMultiFileCommit() throws a CONFLICT-coded error before createTree/createCommit/createRef/updateRef (SHA-mismatch case) or immediately after a rejected createRef/updateRef (ref-race case); no writes are left reachable from any branch (orphaned tree/commit objects are garbage-collected by GitHub); no automatic retry
error_scenarios.user_message: The target file changed since this submission started. Please retry.
error_scenarios.logging: Log the conflicting path(s)/expected-vs-actual SHAs or the ref-race detail tagged [correlationId] from within createMultiFileCommit() itself (its own logger.warn + logMetric('github_api_call', ...) call, §2.4)

error_scenarios.scenario: Git commit succeeds but pull request creation fails
error_scenarios.handling: Return the partial-artifact state (branchName, commitSha) to the caller; do not automatically retry or roll back the commit

error_scenarios.logging: Log branchName and commitSha tagged [correlationId][bundle:bundleId] at error level for manual follow-up

performance.bundle_submission_p95: <=20000ms at 10 environments x 20 distinct secret names (200 encrypt operations)
performance.commit_build_phase: 6 GitHub API calls independent of N (branchExists, getRef, getCommit, createTree, createCommit, createRef/updateRef) plus N parallel write-time CAS reads bounded <=10 (Promise.all getFileContent calls, added Round 1 Blocking Finding 2) — linear in N, not O(1) in isolation, but still bounded and non-quadratic

security: Bundle membership and releaseControlled status are always server-derived from data/secretBundles.json, never trusted from the request body
secretValue never appears in commit messages, PR titles/bodies, exclusion reports, validator error responses, or logMetric payloads at any nesting level

correlationId and bundleId are both included on submitSecretBundleViaGitOps' phase lines (category 1); createMultiFileCommit, createPullRequest, and getFileContent carry correlationId only once threaded through (categories 2-3, no bundleId field exists on these methods); both IDs are present in the final response for a bundle submission; resolveKeyVaults()'s pre-existing, unmodified log lines remain correlationId-only by design (Non-Goal, scope reconciled per Round 1 Blocking Finding 3)
CI secret-leakage grep check is extended to cover the new bundle-mode source paths
reliability: Zero partial-commit-without-PR states except the documented PR_CREATION_FAILED case, which is explicitly surfaced with branchName/commitSha for manual follow-up and never auto-retried
Zero writes on any failure during membership validation, eligibility resolution, encryption, or pre-write conflict detection
Duplicate structural resubmission is rejected via content-addressed branch naming while a distinct submission for the same app+bundle succeeds even with another PR open

No automatic retries on any CONFLICT, whether from the caller's own pre-write/post-encryption re-check, createMultiFileCommit's internal write-time CAS re-read, or a createRef/updateRef 422 ref race (Round 1 Blocking Finding 2) — a single clean failure is always returned, never a silent partial write or silent overwrite
